claims.text: The initial material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloy.
The initial material is in bulk form.
The as-deposited material has relatively large, non-optimized grains.
A short-time subcritical anneal will reduce the grain size.
The anneal-induced grain refinement will increase grain-boundary density.
Increased grain-boundary density will lower local nucleation-energy barriers for the magnetostructural transition.
The refined microstructure will provide a more uniform distribution of nucleation sites.
The refined microstructure will minimize spatial variations in transition-energy barriers.
Lower and more uniform nucleation barriers will broaden the magnetostructural transition.
Lower and more uniform nucleation barriers will reduce magnetostructural-transition hysteresis.
The annealed sample will show a more gradual magnetization change than the as-deposited baseline.
The annealed sample will have a wider transition-temperature range than the as-deposited baseline.
The annealed sample will exhibit less hysteresis during low-field magnetocaloric cycles than the as-deposited baseline.
Rapid quenching after annealing will avoid grain coarsening and unwanted phase transformations.
The predictions apply only if annealing refines the grains below an unspecified critical size without causing grain growth or phase changes.
The predictions apply under low-applied-field magnetic-cooling conditions.
The as-deposited bulk FeMnNiGeSi-type baseline has a sharp, strongly hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
Excess annealing may increase grain size or alter the phase constitution.
Grain growth or phase-constitution changes would negate the intended magnetocaloric improvements.
